title: Compute compact Clifford adjoints and canonical readouts on repeated stabilizer sites
body:
For a supplied affine-quadratic observation at four qubits and width 13, all 256 coefficients of a named symplectic fibre of the true adjoint $A^*y$ form one possibly empty affine-support quadratic-phase chart. A single elimination gives its absolute Gaussian scale, support and phase. This works off the Clifford column span.

For an observation supported at any one raw coordinate, the adjoint has between **5,411,658,792,960 and 8,338,459,852,800 nonzero coefficients**. Both extrema have explicit addresses. The exact count for any other address needs only the 67 subspaces of a four-dimensional binary vector space. Independent literal Clifford-matrix calculations test the counting formula in the two smaller dimensions.

For repeated rank-one stabilizer sites there is a compact **canonical** readout as well. Five rational weights determine the complete Moore–Penrose coefficient vector, including all its phases. The class displacement census on 2,295 Lagrangians and a separate polar-graph character calculation reproduce the same five weights. The squared norm of the projection of a normalized repeated computational coordinate is exactly $478566778595/5856573836677349376$, strictly between zero and one.

This addresses the compact adjoint producer left open by #7816. Ali Romman's affine-quadratic machinery and width-13 conditioning (#5704, #5727, #7772), earlier Clifford sector work and the named-fibre kernels are credited at their source revisions. Unknown tensor-train support discovery in #7815 has a different input interface. The selected conditional exponent remains 0.00363005817.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.
